description: Verify that DUT silently discards an IPv4 packet whose IHL field is less than 5 (header < 20 bytes) — RFC 791 §3.1 mandates IHL >= 5; smaller is malformed
approach:
[Objective]
The IHL field counts the header in 32-bit words; the minimum is 5 (= 20 bytes). A packet with IHL < 5 has a header too short to even hold the mandatory fields, so it must be dropped at the IP layer with no error reply.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: IPv4 packet to DUT IP with IHL < 5 (e.g. IHL=4 = 16 bytes)

2. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: nothing — no reply, no error

[Pass condition]
DUT does not emit any response.

[Fail condition]
Fail_dut_replied — DUT responded despite the malformed IHL. Receive path skipped header-length sanity check.

verdicts.Pass: DUT silently dropped the packet with IHL < 5 — normal
verdicts.Fail_dut_replied: DUT responded despite IHL < 5 — header-length check missing
